title: Safe egress and emergency access
audience: Coordinators, support workers and trained cleaners who may be asked to work in a home affected by hoarding or environmental neglect, as part of an authorised support plan. Not a qualification or authority to clear a property, dispose of a resident's belongings, enter by force, or provide welfare or clinical support.
learningOutcomes: Walk and map the planned evacuation route before any material is staged.
Recognise a blocked exit and stop the affected work.
Record a partly complete job honestly, with the outstanding exit referred.

instruction.heading: Scope of this lesson
instruction.body: This lesson covers mapping and recognising blocked exits. Moving an obstruction is allowed only where the plan authorises that move and the resident agrees. This lesson does not authorise forced entry or structural work.

instruction.heading: Exits are part of the job
instruction.body: The CFA says that hallways, windows and doors can become blocked, and that getting in and out is harder as a result. Blocked routes stop residents from escaping and can stop rescuers reaching people. Before any material is staged, walk the planned route from the main entrance to each exit and to the agreed meeting point. Note trip hazards, narrow passages and any point where a stack or cart could block the way. Keep every route clear of work materials at all times.

instruction.heading: Re-checking and partial completion
instruction.body: Mark the routes on a simple plan agreed with the resident, and recheck them at the start and end of each session and after any change in staging. If a cart or stack blocks the only practical exit during work, stop. Move the obstruction only where the plan authorises that move, and recheck the routes before work continues. A cleared doorway does not finish the job while another exit remains blocked. Record the open exit, record the blocked one, and refer the outstanding hazard.

procedure: Walk the planned route from the entrance to each exit and to the meeting point before staging materials.
Mark the routes and trip hazards on a simple plan agreed with the resident.
Stage material only where it does not reduce the width of any route.
Recheck the routes at the start and end of each session, and after any change.
If an exit becomes blocked, stop, and move an obstruction only where the plan authorises it.
Record the route check and any unresolved exit, and refer it.

workedExamples.situation: A cart is parked in the only practical exit during a break in the work.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop work. Move the cart only if the plan authorises that move and the resident agrees. Recheck the evacuation route before work continues, and record the check.

workedExamples.situation: The bedroom door is clear, but the hallway to the back door is still blocked.
workedExamples.reasoning: The job is partly complete. Record the cleared door, record the blocked exit and refer the outstanding hazard. Do not report the home as fully safe.

equipmentAndPpe: Evacuation-route plan drawn on paper or a tablet and agreed with the resident.
Barrier tape to mark the no-storage zones on the route.
Training-only plan drawings. No real stacks or exits are altered in this lesson.

commonErrors.error: Staging materials in a passage because it is convenient.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep every route clear, and stage only in the approved zones.

commonErrors.error: Assuming one clear exit makes the home safe.
commonErrors.prevention: Check every exit and route, and record the open and blocked ones.

commonErrors.error: Moving stacks to create a path without a competent assessment.
commonErrors.prevention: Withdraw and refer for assessment before any load is moved.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Changes to exits and access must follow the approved plan. This lesson does not authorise forced entry or structural work.
The rules on exit obstructions and fire safety in each state and territory were not checked for this lesson. Check them with the coordinator before any move.

qualityStandard: The learner walks and records the route before work starts.
The learner identifies a blocked exit and stops the affected work.
The learner records a partly complete job honestly.
documentationEvidence: Evacuation-route plan agreed with the resident.
Route-check record at the start and end of each session.
Record of any blocked exit and its referral.
summary: Map every exit and the meeting point first.
Keep routes clear, and stage only in approved zones.
A blocked exit stops the affected work.
One clear doorway does not finish the job.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before materials are staged, what should be done first?
options: Stack the materials by the front door to save time.
Start with the room that has the most items.
Walk the planned route to each exit and to the meeting point.

knowledgeChecks.question: A cart blocks the only practical exit during the work. What is correct?
options: Stop, move the obstruction only where the plan authorises it, and recheck the routes before work continues.
Leave the cart and work around it.
Remove the other stacks to make room for the cart.

knowledgeChecks.question: A bedroom door is clear, but a hallway exit is still blocked. How should the job be recorded?
options: As complete, because a door is clear.
As partly complete, with the blocked exit recorded and referred.
As safe, because the resident has not complained.

officialReferences.title: Hoarding and fire safety (Country Fire Authority, Victoria)
officialReferences.covers: Read through a summary tool on 2026-11-03. The page says clutter can easily catch fire and increase the intensity of a fire; hoarding makes fires more likely to start; hallways, windows and doors can become blocked, so getting in and out is harder; hoarded objects can stop sprinkler water reaching a fire in apartments; one-off clean-ups do not deal with the underlying reasons for hoarding behaviour; and hoarding is a complex issue requiring intervention and long-term support. Publisher: Country Fire Authority (Victoria).

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to enter a home by force, to clear, sort or dispose of a resident's belongings without valid consent, to handle or dispose of hazardous waste, to deal with unstable stacks or structural hazards, or to provide welfare, clinical or safeguarding assessments. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or approval. Work is done only under an authorised support plan and a written agreement with the resident, within the limits set by the employer and the local law. Tenancy, safeguarding and information-sharing rights are jurisdiction-specific, and fire-risk, structural, pest and hazardous-waste decisions belong to the competent authorities and specialists named in the plan. Where authority or consent is unclear, stop and refer.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop and refer whenever any of these is true: consent is not specific, documented and current; the resident has objected or withdrawn consent; a party seeks entry by force, nonconsensual disposal or removal of personal documents; a fire-load, ignition, egress or obstruction hazard is present; a stack or structure is unstable; pests, unknown liquids or mouldy goods are present; sharps, chemicals or unknown containers are found; waste would go to general disposal without characterisation; private information is requested without authority; or the work would go beyond the approved plan. Stopping is a valid professional outcome. Record the disagreement, protect the resident's choices and refer the authority dispute before any property is moved.
